review_note: Granted narrowly. Live Julia test test_poisson_animal_sd_regression.jl: 38 expectations, 0 failures, 0 skips; the 108 manifest entries (checked against a git archive of DRModels.jl at 87a371a66) and the console-log hash match. Oracle: a base-R/Optim dense Laplace objective (_poisson_animal_sd_dense_laplace) with a hand-built A (scaled AR(1) correlation) and a hand-built SD vector exp(alpha0 + alpha1*z) per animal. It is compared with fit.nll(theta) at the true parameters (atol 3e-4), once for the fixture and once for a raw-scale A in a second testset. My Totoro scratch run (Julia 1.10.12, taskset core 164) found fit.nll(theta) minus the oracle of -1.6e-11 against tolerance 3e-4, and oracle gaps of: reversed SD vector 2.9, 1-z flip 4.5, sign-flipped slope 7.1, cov2cor(A) 2.6, 2A 3.7. All are at least about 8,000 times the tolerance. These perturbations are from my scratch run, not asserted in the test. Row support is animal_intercept with A as covariance (the test also checks Ainv equals A, which is only internal parity and is not claimed here). Recovery is sign plus within 0.55 only. Does NOT establish: that the optimiser lands at the oracle optimum (the oracle is evaluated at the true theta), Ainv-precision correctness beyond A-versus-Ainv self-agreement, recovery accuracy beyond one seed, native parity, a slope SD, or interval coverage.
